── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 27, 37, 53, 40 mi
This week: 42 mi over 5 runs.
Feeling: "Anxious about the new date."
Asks: "The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Last week went exactly to plan, and that steady base is what you need now. …
Answers: (1) No, skip the 22. The 20 miler on Sun Sep 13 and the 17 miler last Sunday already give you the endurance this race needs. (2) Two weeks out, a 22 would add fatigue faster than it adds fitness, and the tired legs would carry into the taper. (3) Sunday's 15 miler gives you the same sharpening: 9 easy miles, then 5 miles at marathon pace, then 1 easy mile.
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full rest after the 17 mile long run; sleep is the most useful training you…
Tue: easy, 6 mi, about 9:50/mi and heart rate under 145; finish with four relaxed 20…
Wed: quality, 8 mi, 2 mi easy warm-up, then 4 x 1 mi at 8:35/mi with 2 min easy jog…
Thu: easy, 6 mi, about 9:50/mi and heart rate under 145. Keeps the aerobic base moving…
Fri: rest. Full rest before the long run so you arrive on Sunday fresh.
Sat: easy, 4 mi, about 9:50/mi and heart rate under 145. Short and easy, to loosen up…
Sun: long, 15 mi, 9 mi easy at about 10:00/mi and heart rate under 148, then 5 mi at…
